clue.text: Graduate's determined to get a hound

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate, plus the possessive S
set on something means determined to do it

explanation.surface: A new graduate is resolved to acquire a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is not just grammar: it supplies a letter after the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged breed of hunting dog with long ears.

clue.text: Defender unhappy to concede defeat

blocks.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
feeling down is feeling unhappy

explanation.surface: A dejected defender is forced to admit his team has lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To back down is to withdraw a claim or yield, admitting you cannot win.

clue.text: Some impress us highly, producing a Japanese dish

indicators.note: some means only part, so the letters lie within a longer run of the clue

blocks.note: spans the end of impress, us and the start of highly

explanation.surface: Certain foods greatly impress diners, such as a Japanese speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or vegetables.

clue.text: Ivy, always growing?

blocks.note: ever means always, as in for ever
green describes something young and still growing

explanation.surface: Is ivy constantly spreading?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer's sense of a plant that stays green all year, and Ivy is defined by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy keeps its leaves through winter, so it is an example of a plant that never loses its foliage.

clue.text: This might be produced for chow

definitions.text: This might be produced for chow

blocks.clueFragment: This might be produced for chow
blocks.note: surface reading: something brought out for a chow, the fluffy Chinese dog breed
setter's reading: chow is slang for food, and leftovers from a restaurant meal are boxed up for taking home

explanation.surface: Something made for a pet dog of the chow breed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bag is nominally for the dog, but in practice it carries a diner's uneaten food home, which fits chow as slang for grub.
explanation.definitionFit: A doggy bag is a container for restaurant leftovers, and chow is informal for food.

clue.text: Exaggerations concerning bank documents

blocks.note: over can mean about, as in a row over money
a bank sends statements listing transactions

explanation.surface: Inflated claims about paperwork from the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: An overstatement says more than the truth warrants, the same as an exaggeration.

clue.text: Dogsbody's turn with iron, top of range

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter, so only the start is kept

blocks.note: it is your go means it is your turn
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A household drudge takes a turn ironing, then cooks on the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. A range is an old kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer runs errands for others, and a dogsbody is a British term for someone given menial jobs.

clue.text: Supporter carrying beast turned up — one that snaps

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
an ox is a beast of burden
someone who turned up arrived, that is came

explanation.surface: A fan bearing an animal that has appeared, which then bites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a reversal signal but means arrived. 'One that snaps' suggests a biting animal; snaps here means takes photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A box camera is a simple early camera, and snaps are casual photographs.

clue.text: Wicket taking your spin?

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a wicket is a small gate
yr is the written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: Does the wicket turn for your spin bowler?
explanation.walkthrough: Wicket and spin conjure cricket, but a wicket is also an old word for a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to rotate or whirl round, a synonym of spin as a verb.

clue.text: Bitterness shown over clothes worn by operator in prison

blocks.note: wormwood is a bitter herb, and figuratively bitterness itself
scrubs are the hygienic garments worn by a surgeon operating

explanation.surface: A surgeon's resentment at the gown he is forced to wear in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the first piece above the second. Wormwood Scrubs is a well-known prison in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood Scrubs is the name of an HM men's jail in London, so it is a specific instance of a prison.

clue.text: Stew, as Creoles prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked over and made up, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stew cooked the way Creole people make it.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a slow-cooked dish of meat and vegetables, a kind of stew.

clue.text: One who makes arrangements, with difficulty, to meet the Queen

blocks.note: to be in a fix is to be in difficulty
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: An organiser struggles to set up a meeting with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixer is someone who arranges things, often behind the scenes, an agent or organiser.

clue.text: Impersonating boxer, say, at home, inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a boxer is an example of a breed of dog, as 'say' signals
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Doing an impression of a boxing champion while staying in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is informal for imitating them, as a comedian does a celebrity.

clue.text: Villain tortured miner's cat

indicators.note: something tortured is twisted out of its proper shape

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked person has been cruel to a mining family's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, a synonym of villain.

clue.text: What one queen may have said to the useless jester?

definitions.text: What one queen may have said to the useless jester?

blocks.clueFragment: What one queen may have said
blocks.note: surface reading: a quotation attributed to a monarch, famously Queen Victoria
setter's reading: a jester's job is to make the royal laugh, so failing earns the royal-plural rebuke

explanation.surface: Imagining a monarch's put-down to a jester who is not funny.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous line, attributed to Queen Victoria, uses the royal 'we'; the clue invents an occasion for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock royal expression of disapproval at a failed attempt at humour.

clue.text: Praise daughter in a speech

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the following words

blocks.note: taken as written
an oration is a formal speech
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A father lauds his daughter in a public address.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is worship or deep admiration, as in praise offered to God.

clue.text: Well-informed female, a loser, surprisingly, on the market

indicators.note: something that happens surprisingly comes out in an unexpected way, so the letters fall in a new order

blocks.note: to be up on a subject is to be well-informed about it
F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable woman, unexpectedly a failure, is now being sold off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up for sale is offered to buyers, so it is available on the market.

clue.text: Dramatist shared in production

indicators.note: a production is something put together and staged, so the letters are assembled afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A playwright whose work was jointly staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In production' reads as one phrase, but 'in' joins shared in the mix and 'production' alone signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was an Irish playwright, author of The Rivals and The School for Scandal.

clue.text: Prepared beforehand, she added to cold dish

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made up from raw ingredients, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A cook adds a cold dish she has made in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: The C for cold joins the other words in the shuffle rather than standing apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Corned beef hash is a fried mixture of tinned salt beef, potato and onion, a familiar dish.

clue.text: Frenchman RC male converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French man who became a Roman Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: RC (Roman Catholic) and 'converted' suggest a religious conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel is a common French first name for a man, so it stands for a typical Frenchman.

clue.text: An Alpine snowdrop?

blocks.note: surface reading: a small white flower growing in the mountains
setter's reading: split it into snow and drop, a mass of snow falling down a mountainside

explanation.surface: A wildflower found high in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'snowdrop' should be read as two words, not the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a great mass of snow sliding down a slope, literally snow dropping in mountains like the Alps.

clue.text: A translucent resin included in 'Chambers'

indicators.note: included in means held inside, so the letters sit within the quoted word

blocks.note: sits inside the word, after the first two letters

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry for a resin appears in the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary crossword setters traditionally use, hence the quotation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree resin, golden and translucent, used in jewellery.

clue.text: Consult whistle-blower about returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for about is read the other way

blocks.note: a referee blows the whistle in a match
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Seeking advice from someone who exposes wrongdoing, about coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant, but here it is the match official.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to a book or expert is to consult it for information.

clue.text: Paling, a receiver of stolen goods

blocks.note: first meaning: a barrier of stakes around a field
second meaning: slang for a dealer in loot

explanation.walkthrough: Paling looks like a verb, growing pale, but it is the noun for a fence of stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a barrier like a paling, and in criminal slang a person who handles stolen property.

clue.text: Rise in status of Conservative party

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a limb is a branch or wing of an organisation, here taken as a party

explanation.surface: A politician's promotion within the Conservative Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Party for limb is loose: a limb is a branch of a larger body, as a wing is part of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to advance socially or professionally, as in climbing the ladder.

clue.text: United ran out in green

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in proper place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A United footballer runs out wearing a green strip.
explanation.walkthrough: United looks like a team name or the abbreviation U; all six letters go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or new to something, so someone green is not yet trained.

clue.text: Extended break using snooker aid

blocks.note: first meaning: a lengthy period of repose
second meaning: the extra-long cue support used for distant shots in snooker

explanation.surface: A snooker player builds a long run of pots with the help of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: A break in snooker is a scoring run, which makes the first meaning look like part of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest is a pause and a long one is extended; snooker players also use a long-handled rest to bridge the cue.

clue.text: Number crossing mouth of Romanian river

indicators.note: a mouth is the opening at the front, so only the start of the word is kept
crossing means straddling, so one piece spans the other

blocks.note: seven is a number
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Many people crossing the mouth of a river in Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: Mouth suggests an estuary, fitting the river scene, but it just takes a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England to the Bristol Channel.
